posts.title: Ef4：Visual Design
posts.content:
1. Tech Stack
p5.js: canvas, drawing, animation loop
p5.sound: audio loading and FFT analysis
Assets: one cyberpunk image (cyberpunk_image.jpg) and one Y2K-style track (y2k_track.mp3)
UI: black background, pixel font (Press Start 2P), minimal player bar

2. Particle System (Core Visual)
Source: The image is sampled on a grid with step size dotSize = 8. Each sample becomes one particle.
Particle data: Each particle stores
initial position (x0, y0)
current position (x, y) and velocity (vx, vy)
color (r, g, b), alpha, base size
a seed used for Perlin noise
Y2K color: Original RGB is remapped (e.g. green reduced with g * 0.6) so the palette leans purple/pink/cyan and feels Y2K.

3. Motion and Forces
Each frame, every particle gets three force components, then position is updated:
Spring (return force)
Force = k * (x0 - x), with k tied to audio.
Pulls particles back to their initial positions so they “spread and snap back”.
Perlin noise
noise(seed + t) and noise(seed + 100 + t) give (nx, ny).
Scaled by CHAOS_STRENGTH for smooth, organic drift without random jitter.
Mouse repulsion
Within MOUSE_RADIUS = 120, particles are pushed away from the cursor along the “particle → mouse” direction.
Stronger when closer; strength also scales with audio level, so the “mouse pushes particles” effect reacts to the music.
Velocity is damped (e.g. vx = (vx + fx) * 0.88) for smooth motion.

4. Audio Link
p5.FFT analyzes the playing track and reads bass energy.
Bass is smoothed with lerp(smoothedBass, bass, 0.12) to avoid jitter.
The smoothed bass value drives:
Spring strength k: stronger music → stronger spring → more “bouncy” motion.
Particle size: sz = baseSize * (0.5 + 2.8 * audioForce) so particles grow with the beat.
Mouse repulsion: slightly stronger when the music is louder.
So: strong bass → bigger, more active, bouncier particles; weak bass → smaller, calmer motion.

5. Rendering and Performance
Each particle is drawn as a small rectangle (rect) with color and alpha from the sampled pixel.
When performance allows (canvas area under a threshold), rectangles get shadow (ctx.shadowBlur, shadowColor) for a glow.
On large canvases the sketch:
Caps internal resolution (e.g. max 1600×960)
Lowers particle count (e.g. from 500 to 360)
Disables shadow
to keep the frame rate acceptable.

6. Layout and UI
style.css: black background, neon CSS variables (pink, cyan, red), pixel-style buttons and title.
Canvas uses about 75% width and 82% height of the window; below it are the “PIXEL VISUAL” title and PLAY/PAUSE button in a minimal player layout.
